title: Square Miles Calculator: Drawn Region Areas
description: Measure a drawn region's area in square miles with the Square Miles Calculator — regions, parks and study zones, with other units alongside. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, New York's Central Park measures 843 acres — 1.317 square miles, the drawn-region arithmetic this calculator performs on any outline you give it.
quick_answer: The Square Miles Calculator measures the area of a region you draw or define, reported in square miles with acres and square kilometres alongside. Draw the boundary for a park, study zone or territory and read its true ground area — not the bounding box's flattering overestimate.

faq: How exact is a drawn area?
As exact as the boundary you trace and the data under it. Points placed carefully on a good map give areas good to a fraction of a percent — plenty for planning, short of legal survey.
Your outline decides: trace the shoreline for land area, the full boundary for total. Published 'areas' mix conventions; yours can state its own.
Yes — the result reports the family together (acres, sq mi, km², hectares) because audiences differ.
Draw each part and add — or the map's region tools handle multi-polygons where supported. The arithmetic is addition either way.
Why not just use the official figure?
When one exists and suits, do. Drawing earns its keep for custom regions — study zones, proposed districts, your own boundary that no office has measured.
Boundary follows a river's centre or bank?
Your trace, your convention — centre-line is the survey habit. State the choice next to the number.
Zoom in and trace carefully; the calculator's arithmetic is scale-free, and small polygons deserve the same vertex care as counties.
Always — the outline is editable until the area is quoted; after quoting, save the outline beside the number so the figure stays reproducible.
